notes.title: POSSIBLE FINAL UPDATE
notes.notes:
This is very likely going to be the final update for Atlas Ablaze. Admittedly, I had plans to add additional artwork to the game, but after a while I realized that it feels complete as it is.

     Regardless of me saying this, feel free to let me know if you notice any typos, grammatical errors, bugs, ect. as I'm still willing to update the game if anyone really wants me to clean any other parts of it up. That being said, as a newer game developer, there are some issues that are common within the engine I use that I don't know how to fix.

     Please keep this in mind, because I've tried my best to make a game that works smoothly, but there are certain things I just don't know how to polish. For example, if you skip too often, the game may freeze. If this happens, by the way, you should NOT overwrite your last save in a spot where the game froze. It will not work properly.

     Thank you to anyone who supported my passion project. It means a lot to me.

notes.title: MESSAGE BOX FONT UPDATED
notes.notes:
Here's the update, later than expected but it's here!
I toyed with the idea of letting the player select one of two fonts, but that is very much out of my range of skills. Instead, I altered the font of the character dialogue to be easier to read.

Minor updates that come with this:
-I fixed a few typos
-A small line of dialogue was changed, but it isn't important enough for players to have to dig around for it

Anyways, I hope this makes everything easier to read!

notes.title: Additional Font Options Being Tested
notes.notes:
One thing I'm told a lot about my game is that the font can be difficult to read, however, I really like the aesthetic of it and I know I'm not alone in that.

I'll be playing around with some ways I can program in [b][u]an option to change the font to something easier to read[/u][/b], but it'll still be pixelated and [b][u]will probably only apply to the message box[/u][/b] where dialogue between characters shows up. The current font I use will be the default.

I'm not sure how long it'll take me as I'm still fairly new to game development. It seems like a simple yet tedious thing to add in. I apologize for not doing something like this sooner!! I'm going to start working on it ASAP.

Thank you in advance for your patience as I continue to learn! And if you're not so patient, well- *cries until I throw up.*ːsteamthumbsdownːːsteamthumbsdownːːsteamthumbsdownː

notes.title: Atlas Ablaze Demo Update
notes.notes:
You read that right, new content is available in the Atlas Ablaze demo! Wooooo!

It should look the same at first glance, but try playing through an entire scene then moving forward to the next scene. There's some sneaky little uh, some sneaky uhm, I snuck some uhhhh stuff in between the main scenes.
And you may be thinking, "It's not sneaky if you tell us about it!" To that I say, you're right. I know. I'm just being dramatic but you should definitely check it out.

I felt like the demo was too lighthearted in comparison to the full game, so I wanted to fix that without dropping any major spoilers. If you play it, tell me what you think!

Oh, and Brad hating? Smoother than ever now. Best it's ever been. You can now hate on Brad with even more ease.

notes.title: Atlas Ablaze Demo is in Progress!
notes.notes:
I'm working on a free demo for Atlas Ablaze that'll include some of the scenes in the game to give players a feel of how it's written.

The demo will NOT include consequences, big spoilers, or any scenes where the player would use Andi's phone to progress. If you have any questions about what to expect in the full version of the game, I suggest either checking the "about this game," section of the store page. You can also email me with any questions you have and I'll try to get back to you quickly.

Hopefully the demo will be out in a few days.
